title: QatarEnergy announces/resumes LNG production in Qatar by April 30?
description:
QatarEnergy, a Qatari state-owned petroleum company, announced on March 2 that it would halt production of liquefied natural gas (LNG) due to military strikes on its operating facilities (see: https://www.qatarenergy.qa/en/MediaCenter/Pages/newsdetails.aspx?ItemId=3892).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if QatarEnergy resumes production of liquefied natural gas at QatarEnergy LNG production facilities in Qatar, or officially announces that such production has resumed or will resume, by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

QatarEnergy resuming the production of other halted products, including downstream LNG-related products, or resuming transportation of LNG without resuming production, will not alone count.

An official announcement that LNG production will resume at QatarEnergy LNG production facilities in Qatar must signal the end of the total LNG production halt effective immediately or on a specific date or clearly defined time window. Mere statements that production will resume at some undefined point in the future, or that production will resume once the halt has ended, will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from QatarEnergy (https://www.qatarenergy.qa/en/Pages/vHome.aspx); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on QatarEnergy announcing or resuming LNG production in Qatar by April 30 reflects near-certainty following the early April 2026 ceasefire amid Strait of Hormuz tensions and prior missile attacks on Ras Laffan facilities, which prompted a March production halt and force majeure declarations. Reuters and industry reports confirmed preparations starting April 8, with partial restarts of select trains at Ras Laffan by mid-April, enabling initial output amid global supply concerns. This skin-in-the-game assessment prices Yes shares at 99.8%, as scaling to full capacity remains procedural rather than uncertain. eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices France (16.4%) narrowly ahead of Spain (15.3%) for the 2026 FIFA World Cup title, reflecting their dominant qualifier campaigns and depth amid an injury crisis hitting stars like Kylian Mbappé's hamstring issue and Rodri's extended recovery, which tempers outright favoritism. Defending champions Argentina (8.6%) and Brazil (8.6%) trail closely on resurgent form post-qualifiers, bolstered by Lionel Messi's experience and Brazil's rebound under new management, while England (11.1%) and Portugal (7.3%) benefit from favorable group draws separating top seeds until semifinals. The 48-team expanded format, playoff drama concluding in late March, and balanced group stage matchups—such as France vs. Norway/Senegal, Spain vs. Uruguay—fuel tight odds, emphasizing upset potential and knockout volatility over the June-July tournament across North America.

title: Counter-Strike: Natus Vincere vs FaZe (BO3) - BLAST Rivals Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the Counter-Strike Semifinal 1 match between Natus Vincere and FaZe in the BLAST Rivals Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 2 at 1:30PM ET.

This market will resolve to "Natus Vincere" if Natus Vincere win the match against FaZe.

This market will resolve to "FaZe" if FaZe win the match against Natus Vincere.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. However, if https://hltv.org has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Natus Vincere enters the BLAST Rivals Spring 2026 playoffs BO3 semifinal against FaZe Clan as the clear trader consensus favorite, driven by their dominant group stage run including a 2-0 opener over lower-ranked opponents and consistent roster firepower from makazze (top-3 VRS player), w0nderful, iM, Aleksib, and b1t. FaZe, ranked around #40, barely advanced via upsets against G2 and FURIA but struggled with a transitional lineup after karrigan's departure to Falcons, neitu as stand-in, Twistzz shifting to IGL duties, and new coach enkay J—resulting in uneven performances. Head-to-head favors NaVi 6-4 over recent CS2 maps, with Ancient and Dust2 likely deciders in this high-stakes single-elimination bracket at Dickies Arena, where NaVi's momentum and map control edge prevail amid no reported roster absences.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen lead trader consensus at 33.7% implied probability for Eurovision 2026 victory with their violin-pop fusion "Liekinheitin," a standout since winning UMK in March amid strong fan polls and balanced jury-televote appeal. Greece's Akylas follows at 19.1% as a jury frontrunner with edgy "Ferto," bolstered by pre-rehearsal buzz and Balkan vote potential, while Denmark's solid entry holds 12.6% on Nordic momentum. The wide-open field reflects rehearsal uncertainties in Vienna—first sessions underway as of May 2—plus televote threats from Israel and Australia, with semis on May 12-14 poised to shift dynamics amid OGAE poll dominance by Finland.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 F1 Drivers' standings at 75 points ahead of the Miami Grand Prix, holding a slim seven-point edge over teammate George Russell (68) after back-to-back wins in China and Japan, fueling his 35% trader consensus as title favorite. Antonelli's blistering qualifying pace—claiming pole for Sunday's Miami Grand Prix—and superior average finish (1.33) underscore Mercedes' early-season dominance, with the silver arrows locking out prediction market top spots. Russell's consistency and experience keep him close at 28%, but intra-team tension intensifies amid a long championship grind, while Leclerc (55 points), Norris, and Verstappen trail amid weaker constructor pace, leaving room for upgrades to shake up the tightly bunched leader board.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance holds a slim edge in trader consensus for the 2028 presidential election winner at 21.6% implied probability on Polymarket, buoyed by his role as heir apparent to President Trump and solid GOP primary positioning, though recent April 2026 polls like UMass Lowell show his head-to-head lead over Gavin Newsom narrowing to 33%-30%. California Governor Newsom trails closely at 17.6%, gaining from his strong Democratic nominee odds (over 25%) and national visibility via policy clashes with the administration, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio's 10.1% reflects rising buzz from foreign policy maneuvers like Venezuela operations. The fragmented field and lack of formal campaigns keep the race tight ahead of pivotal 2026 midterms, which could signal incumbency backlash or momentum; economic trends, Trump endorsements, or scandals may create separation.

title: Elon Musk # tweets April 28 - May 5, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from April 28 12:00 PM ET to May 5, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

Final days (May 3-5) hold swing potential amid xAI momentum and political engagement, where any surge in cultural commentary could tip toward higher bins, underscoring prediction markets' skin-in-the-game wisdom on Musk's unpredictable social media cadence.

eventMetadata.context_description: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. leads trader consensus at 49% implied probability for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, fueled by his visible Make America Healthy Again push—including April congressional testimony defending HHS budget cuts and panel overhauls—and a base-rallying midterm travel effort on April 4 that broadens his populist appeal beyond traditional lanes. Vice President J.D. Vance follows at 39%, leveraging incumbency and a March CPAC straw poll win, though prediction markets diverge from recent polls showing stronger support for him. Secretary of State Marco Rubio at 21% gains from donor "draft" momentum and foreign policy prominence amid March Iran escalations, underscoring a fluid post-Trump primary field tested by 2026 midterms.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Jordan Bardella's edge over Édouard Philippe in trader consensus reflects late March 2026 polls placing the Rassemblement National leader atop first-round intentions at 34-38%, with Philippe at 18-25% amid a fragmented center-right field including Retailleau, Attal, and Wauquiez, plus divided left options like Mélenchon and Glucksmann. Marine Le Pen trails due to her 2025 embezzlement ban. Primaries, endorsements, or economic shifts could consolidate votes and tip the closely contested 2027 race.

title: Will the Iranian regime fall by May 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 97.4% for the Iranian regime falling by May 31, reflecting its resilience amid the 2026 war with U.S. and Israeli airstrikes, widespread protests suppressed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and a smooth leadership transition after Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's death on February 28 to his son Mojtaba on March 8. Recent April 30 statements from Mojtaba Khamenei on Gulf diplomacy and negotiation proposals signal institutional continuity despite economic collapse and proxy conflicts, with no verified mass defections or uprisings in the past 30 days. Scenarios that could shift odds include sudden IRGC fractures, opposition-led revolts backed by external actors, or escalated strikes crippling command structures, though historical patterns favor regime survival through coercion.

title: LoL: Cloud9 vs Dignitas (BO3) - LCS Regular Season
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between Cloud9 and Dignitas in the LCS Regular Season, initially scheduled for May 2 at 4:00PM ET.

This market will resolve to "Cloud9" if Cloud9 win the match against Dignitas.

This market will resolve to "Dignitas" if Dignitas win the match against Cloud9.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

markets.description:

This market will resolve to "Over" if the total kills in Game 1 is 24 or more. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Under".

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cloud9 holds the top spot in LCS Spring Split regular season standings at 4-0 series record and 8-2 games entering this BO3 matchup, with recent dominant wins over Shopify Rebellion (2-0) and Disguised (2-0) underscoring their macro strength and individual carry potential from stars like Zven and Blaber. eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil spot price settled at $101.94 per barrel on May 1, 2026, down nearly 3% from $105.07, driven by trader optimism for a US-Iran ceasefire easing prior Strait of Hormuz disruptions and Middle East infrastructure strikes that spiked prices above $105. OPEC+ approved a modest 206,000 barrels per day output quota increase for May, countering supply constraints amid backwardation in futures curves signaling near-term tightness. EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts Brent peaking at $115/bbl in Q2 2026 before declining on ample non-OPEC supply growth. Key catalysts include weekly EIA inventory reports, potential geopolitical flare-ups, and IEA's May 13 Oil Market Report, shaping end-month price dynamics.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 5 - May 12, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from May 5 12:00 PM ET to May 12, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

title: LoL: FURIA Esports vs RED Canids (BO3) - CBLOL Regular Season
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between FURIA Esports and RED Canids in the CBLOL Regular Season, initially scheduled for May 2 at 3:00PM ET.

This market will resolve to "FURIA Esports" if FURIA Esports win the match against RED Canids.

This market will resolve to "RED Canids" if RED Canids win the match against FURIA Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

title: Trump announces US blockade of Hormuz lifted by...?
description:
On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump imposed a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in mid-April 2026 following collapsed peace talks with Iran, aiming to pressure Tehran on nuclear negotiations and curb its regional influence amid escalating tensions. As of May 2, the blockade persists despite Iran briefly closing the strait in response and recently proposing to reopen shipping lanes in exchange for lifting the US measures on Iranian ports, an offer Trump rejected as insufficient without broader concessions. Diplomatic signals remain mixed, with Trump declaring hostilities "terminated" yet sustaining economic warfare via sanctions warnings to shipping firms paying Iranian tolls. Surging oil prices and global supply disruptions underscore the stakes, while upcoming talks could tip trader consensus on resolution timelines.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: A fragile US-Iran ceasefire, mediated by Pakistan since early April 2026, persists without progress toward a permanent peace deal following stalled Islamabad talks. President Trump's administration rejected Iran's latest two-phase proposal on May 1, which sought to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease sanctions before addressing nuclear curbs and ballistic missiles—core US red lines demanding verifiable non-proliferation commitments. Deep mistrust, rooted in the 2018 JCPOA collapse and ongoing regional tensions, sustains trader skepticism amid economic fallout from the blockade and war. No new negotiations are scheduled, though UN Security Council involvement or midterm pressures could prompt diplomatic shifts before any resolution deadline.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 1 - May 8, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from May 1 12:00 PM ET to May 8, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

eventMetadata.context_description: Pittsburgh Pirates carry momentum into game two at PNC Park after a 9-1 rout of NL Central-leading Cincinnati Reds (20-12) yesterday, snapping a five-game skid behind Ryan Davis's two homers and Mitch Keller's seven strong innings. Carmen Mlodzinski (1-2, 4.13 ERA) takes the hill for the Pirates (17-16, fourth-ranked NL team ERA at 3.74) against Rhett Lowder (3-1, 3.18 ERA) in a matchup favoring Pittsburgh's home advantage and season series edge (3-1). Reds boast a 10-4 road record and hot Elly De La Cruz (10 HR), but recent 6-4 last-10 form shows pitching vulnerabilities; minimal injuries like Eugenio Suarez's oblique sideline both sides' key pieces. Cool 45-degree weather could suppress offense in this closely contested divisional clash.

eventMetadata.context_description: US-Iran direct talks in Islamabad on April 11-12 marked the highest-level face-to-face diplomacy since 1979, with US envoys including VP JD Vance and Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi negotiating a ceasefire, nuclear curbs, and Strait of Hormuz access, but ended in impasse after 21 hours without agreement. President Trump subsequently ordered a US blockade of Iranian ports, escalating tensions. Iran's latest proposal on April 28 to reopen the Strait while postponing nuclear discussions drew US rejection over unresolved enrichment issues. No second round is scheduled amid mutual recriminations, though mediators like Pakistan and Oman continue efforts; traders watch for de-escalation signals or military developments that could prompt renewed negotiations before any resolution deadline.
